posts.author: Cristiano_Perrucci
posts.content_md:
A few months ago I started experimentation with a laser cannibalized from a DVD burner. 

I shot several holos but all shown rings due to mode-hops. I tried to stabilize the temperature with a generous heat-sink without any improvement. 

This week I've finished to build a closed-loop TEC control (based on MAX1968 integrated circuit and a NTC) that allows laser temperature stability within 0.01C. 

The question is: 

What is the minimum wavelength stability for holographic purpose? 

Attached you find the laser diode behaviour (constant current, Pout=80mW) without TEC and with TEC in closed-loop configuration. 

Measurements are done with a Anritsu MS710C Opt. Spectr. Analizer. coupling the free-space optical signal to a single mode 9um fiber. 

![Image](http://digilander.libero.it/crispers/bboardlaser/ld660nmMM.gif)

![Image](http://digilander.libero.it/crispers/bboardlaser/ld660nmSM.gif)

posts.author: dcgman
posts.content_md:
from your second chart, I see that the full width of the curve at half power (i.e. 6dB below the max) is approximately 0.3nm. This is your figure for delta lambda

coherence length=(lambda squared) divided by (delta lambda)

So the coherence length of the cooled laser diode is 1.4mm

- 250 x 250 mm MBDCG plate

- 7 mins exposure time (the plate was evenly exposed)

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
Wow, that looks nice and compact. Did you mount the bottom of the laser unit to a large heat sink? You need a thermal mass that is several times larger than the mass on the laser side of the peltier.

Also, I noticed that you don't use shielded/grounded cables for feedback of temperature and feed-forward of laser diode current. It's important to use shielded cables in both cases to make sure there is no cross-talk from the highly noisy high current that goes through the peltier and the temperature feedback.

I noticed that you use only two terminals of the laser diode. So no power sensing feedback. That is very good. But just to make sure, you do supply the diode constant current, yes?

If you have good temperature stability and shielded cables, you should be able to get coherence length of several meters with powers up to about 40mW.

Ah, I just noticed you use a constant current source with a single transistor. Please bear in mind that they are quite sensitive to changes in ambient temperature. Did you measure the current through the diode for a longer period of time?

posts.author: Cristiano_Perrucci
posts.content_md:
> **Colin Kaminski:** Nice work! Keep us updated with results.Here is MaximDallas's website:http://www.maxim-ic.com/Do you have a schematic you can post?

Sorry for the hand drawn schematic, I worked for many years with a CAD software, so when I' playing with my toys I prefere the old method... each time I'm approaching to Eagle PCB, Orcad PCB and so on, I'm feeling like suffering from an allergy! 

![Image](http://digilander.libero.it/crispers/bboardlaser/bboard.gif)

> **Hans:** Wow, that looks nice and compact. Did you mount the bottom of the laser unit to a large heat sink? You need a thermal mass that is several times larger than the mass on the laser side of the peltier.

As far as the temperature difference between the two faces of the TEC is small, I don't need a big heat sink to dissipate heat. For the preliminary experiments, LD temp is close to room temperature, so the peltier drinks only a few tens of milliamps. Note that the element I'm using is very small, on the other hand the butterfly case I used is much bigger than the active element. See the picture of the laser housing before dissection:

![Image](http://digilander.libero.it/crispers/bboardlaser/butterfly.jpg)

> Also, I noticed that you don't use shielded/grounded cables for feedback of temperature and feed-forward of laser diode current. It's important to use shielded cables in both cases to make sure there is no cross-talk from the highly noisy high current that goes through the peltier and the temperature feedback.

As stated the current flowing in the TEC is very small, also, the TEC control works at 500KHz while the loop bandwidth has a low cut-off frequency. The final version will be connectorized with adequate wiring connections.

> I noticed that you use only two terminals of the laser diode. So no power sensing feedback. That is very good. But just to make sure, you do supply the diode constant current, yes?

I know this is a big lacuna. Unfortunally the laser diode lacks of the embedded monitor photodiode! Anyway the LD is driven by a constant current circuit.

> If you have good temperature stability and shielded cables, you should be able to get coherence length of several meters with powers up to about 40mWAh, I just noticed you use a constant current source with a single transistor. Please bear in mind that they are quite sensitive to changes in ambient temperature. Did you measure the current through the diode for a longer period of time?

The reference voltage of the pump current is very stable. With quite stable room temperature, the current drift due to the junction temperature changes is very small (<0.1mA over 30 minutes)
